chunks.arabic_text: الكَافِي: عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ، عَنْ وَهيبِ بْنِ حَفْصٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Wahib ibn Hafs, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كُنَّا مَعَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ فَآتَاهُ عَمْرُو بْنُ إِلْيَاسَ فَقَالَ لَهُ: يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ، إِنَّ أَخِي بِحَلَبَ بَعَثَ إِلَيَّ بِمَالٍ مِنَ الزَّكَاةِ أَقْسِمُهُ بِالْكُوفَةِ، فَقَطَعَ عَلَيْهِ الطَّرِيقَ، فَهَلْ عِنْدَكَ فِيهِ رِوَايَةٌ؟ فَقَالَ: نَعَمْ. سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ، وَلَمْ أَظُنَّ أَنَّ أَحَدًا يَسْأَلُنِي عَنْهَا أَبَدًا، فَقُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: جَعَلْتُكَ فَدَاكَ، الرَّجُلُ يَبْعَثُ بِزَكَاتِهِ مِنْ أَرْضٍ إِلَى أَرْضٍ، فَيُقْطَعُ عَلَيْهِ الطَّرِيقَ، فَقَالَ: قَدْ أَجْزَأَتْ عَنْهُ، وَلَوْ كُنْتُ أَنَا لَأَعَدَّهَا

translations.en: We were with Abi Basir when Amr ibn Ilyas came to him and said to him: O Aba Muhammad, my brother is in Halab (Aleppo), he sent me some wealth as Zakat to distribute it in Kufa, but the road was cut off on him [it was stolen/lost], do you have a narration about this? He said: Yes. I asked Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) about this matter, and I did not think that anyone would ever ask me about it, so I said to Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, a man sends his Zakat from one land to another, but it is intercepted on the road, he said: It is sufficient for him [he is excused], and if it were me, I would repeat it [give it again].

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'ajza'at 'anhu' (exemption from re-payment) when Zakat funds are lost in transit, illustrating the Imam's balance between strict legal obligation and voluntary generosity (ihtiyat or infaq). It serves as a key example of the authority of solitary reports (khabar al-wahid) from truthful narrators like Abu Basir, reinforcing their reliability in deriving fiqh rulings. The Imam’s personal inclination to pay again underscores the distinction between the minimum legal requirement and the higher standard of spiritual excellence.
en.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zakat if the money is lost or stolen before reaching the poor?

key_terms.أَجْزَأَتْ عَنْهُ: It is sufficient for him / obligation fulfilled
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), referring to Imam al-Baqir
